claims.text: Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits increasing friction at elevated temperature.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits increasing wear at elevated temperature.
A controlled pre-oxidation or surface-activation treatment will induce a nanostructured protective oxide layer during initial sliding.
The induced oxide nanolayer will contain self-organized oxide phases that remain stable from room temperature to 800 °C.
The induced oxide nanolayer will act as a lubricious tribofilm.
The oxide nanolayer will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
The oxide nanolayer's nanoscale morphology and high-temperature stability will mitigate adhesive wear.
The oxide nanolayer's nanoscale morphology and high-temperature stability will mitigate abrasive wear.
The oxide nanolayer will lower interfacial shear stress under thermally activated sliding conditions.
Treated CoCrFeNi will have a lower and more stable coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout 25–800 °C.
Treated CoCrFeNi will have lower wear depth or wear rate than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout 25–800 °C.
The treatment's tribological benefit may be maintained or enhanced as temperature approaches 800 °C.
The elevated-temperature friction and wear of untreated CoCrFeNi are caused by tribo-oxidation and degradation of its native surface.
The proposed operating scope is sliding in ambient air under controlled loads from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
Performance above 800 °C, in non-oxidizing environments, or under substantially different stresses remains untested.
The oxide layer's phase composition, thickness, formation kinetics, and long-term durability are uncertain.
